title: Natural Q&A #3
summary: NH answers leftover viewer questions about his university background, subliminals, Roko's basilisk and AI, whether serious lifters struggle socially, mindfulness, and why he refuses to monetize the channel. He ends with book recommendations and his view on the lifelong playboy lifestyle versus settling down.
claims: He holds a double degree in literature and communication plus a literature-related master's he will not name, to protect his anonymity
He preferred high school to his bachelor's; the low level and lack of structure let him coast for three years, then a very competitive master's forced a crash course
His scholarship meant he had to finish the master's in exactly two years
Academia is toxic and passive-aggressive; he never wants to go back for a PhD
He has never used subliminals or binaural beats; whatever they do is self-suggestion, which you can do yourself by repeating positive thoughts and acting on them
Manifestation is not a prayer: you go out and get it
He will not believe subliminals grow height or body parts without footage proving it
The only things that raise testosterone for naturals are training, a less toxic environment, a pure mindset, and diet
He works in AI; Roko's basilisk is a good logic exercise but will never happen because it assumes an AI with a sense of good and evil and self-will
AI only does what its programmers taught it; it cannot learn outside that scope the way humans do
You do not need a STEM degree to work in AI; teams include people with master's degrees in history and languages
Being a serious lifter starts at around 8-10 hours a week in the gym, enough that training replaces hobbies or social time
Serious lifters do struggle socially because friends and partners will not understand skipping a night out for a big bench day
He is a strong introvert from a family of extroverts; people drain him and he needs solitude to recharge
Training versus seeing loved ones is not really a choice, it is deciding what matters most in your life
Social pressure to go to bars and clubs can push young people to stop training, which harms their lives
He does not meditate; training is his meditation and his mind is mostly quiet unless he chooses to think
He will never monetize the channel: ad revenue is negligible without millions of monthly views
Not monetizing avoids content claims, spares viewers ads, and keeps him independent of views, metrics and viewer demands
If the channel became a job he would lose pleasure and quit; he refuses sponsorships too
His three book recommendations: The Book of Five Rings, Hagakure and Marcus Aurelius's Meditations
AI is not overhyped but underhyped, because knowledge taught to machines is reusable and grows exponentially
No one wants to die alone; avoid any path of life leading there, which is also why immortality is overrated
What the viewer calls polyamory is really just being a lifelong bachelor; polyamory exists within a couple
Serial casual dating leaves a wake of hurt partners and involves lies; he considers it immoral and soul-rotting
From a biological standpoint the deeper meaning of life is passing on your genes; marriage sugarcoats that
He started dating late in his 20s, had wild years in his early 20s, found it did not make him happy, and is now happily monogamous
Being a man rather than a male means mastering and repressing your urges, a mastery men should attain early in their 20s

which master's to work in AI
dying alone after a playboy lifestyle
